title: RÝNI Helm chart values
description: Privacy-preserving, self-hosted web analytics (PocketBase backend + SolidJS frontend served by nginx). This schema describes every value the chart reads. It is intentionally permissive: unknown keys are ignored, and no value is required, so existing values files keep working. Artifact Hub renders this file as the chart's documented values table; Helm validates user values against the closed sets (enums) below on install and upgrade.

nameOverride.description: Override the chart name (used in resource naming).

fullnameOverride.description: Override the fully-qualified app name (used in resource naming).

namespace.description: Namespace the chart installs into. The chart can optionally create it. Pick ONE: `namespace.create: true` or `helm install --create-namespace` with `namespace.create: false` — using both can race.

create.description: Whether to create the namespace. The namespace is annotated `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`, so `helm uninstall` never deletes it.

name.description: Name of the namespace to install into.

image.description: Settings shared by both container images.

pullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets, passed verbatim as `imagePullSecrets` on both pod specs and the ServiceAccount. Each item is a Kubernetes LocalObjectReference, i.e. `- name: regcred`. Empty for public docker.io images; set this for a private registry.

name.description: Name of the pull secret in the release namespace.

pullPolicy.description: Image pull policy applied to both containers unless the per-image `pullPolicy` overrides it.

serviceAccount.description: ServiceAccount configuration. Both pods reference this SA; no RBAC is attached today, but the SA is created explicitly so future hooks (or external-secrets operators) can bind roles to it.

name.description: ServiceAccount name. If empty, the chart uses the fullname.

pocketbase.description: PocketBase backend (single replica; sqlite is not HA-capable).

replicaCount.description: Number of PocketBase replicas. Keep at 1: sqlite on a ReadWriteOnce volume is not HA-capable.

tag.description: PocketBase image tag. Should match the RÝNI release (e.g. v0.1.0).

pullPolicy.description: Image pull policy for PocketBase. Empty falls back to `image.pullPolicy`.

service.description: PocketBase Service. The container always listens on 8090; `port` only changes the Service port (targetPort: http), so probes and the listener never disagree.

port.description: Port exposed by the PocketBase service.

persistence.description: PocketBase stores everything in a single sqlite `data.db` (sites, page-view records, and heartbeats). Analytics data grows slowly — a few Gi is plenty for most self-hosted installs.

enabled.description: Whether to create a PVC for the PB data directory. When false, PB data lives in an emptyDir and is lost when the pod is recreated.

storageClass.description: Storage class name. IMPORTANT: the StorageClass must have `reclaimPolicy: Retain` if you want the underlying PV (and your data) to survive PVC deletion. The chart annotates the PVC with `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` for the Helm lifecycle, but the PV's fate is the StorageClass's decision.

resources.description: PocketBase holds the sqlite page cache and JSVM pools in memory; 256Mi is a comfortable floor for typical analytics workloads.

healthcheck.description: Health check path used by the startup, liveness and readiness probes.

path.description: Health check path (PB exposes /api/health). Probes always target the container port 8090.

startupProbe.description: startupProbe tuning: allows up to failureThreshold * periodSeconds (default 150s) for the first boot (migrations, superuser upsert) before the liveness probe takes over.

failureThreshold.description: Failed startup probe attempts tolerated before the container is restarted.

superuserIps.description: Superuser login allowlist (space-separated IPs/CIDRs), passed as PB_SUPERUSER_IPS and applied by entrypoint.sh on every start. Empty = no restriction. NOTE: behind an ingress PB sees the ingress controller's pod IP unless PB's trusted proxy settings are configured, so restrict to client ranges only after configuring those.

automigrate.description: PB_AUTOMIGRATE. Default false because the container root filesystem is read-only and migration files generated from dashboard edits would be lost on restart anyway. Shipped migrations are always applied on start regardless of this flag.

secret.description: PB_SECRET source. EITHER supply an existing Secret (name + key), OR leave both empty and the chart will auto-generate a Secret on install. PB_SECRET is the AES key for the encrypted `data.db`; the chart re-uses it via `lookup` on upgrade, so it must never rotate.

existingSecret.description: Name of an existing Kubernetes Secret containing PB_SECRET. If empty, the chart auto-generates one as a regular release resource that is re-used on upgrade (lookup) and kept on uninstall (resource-policy).

existingSecretKey.description: Key inside `existingSecret` that holds the PB_SECRET value.

superuser.description: First superuser credentials. The Secret is mounted into the pod as PB_SUPERUSER_EMAIL / PB_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD and entrypoint.sh creates the superuser headlessly on the first boot. Leave empty to auto-generate. PB requires the password to be at least 8 characters.

existingSecret.description: Name of an existing Kubernetes Secret holding PB_SUPERUSER_EMAIL and PB_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD. If empty, the chart creates one on install with a random 24-char password.

existingSecretEmailKey.description: Key inside `existingSecret` that holds the email value.

existingSecretPasswordKey.description: Key inside `existingSecret` that holds the password value.

podSecurityContext.description: Pod-level securityContext for the PocketBase pod.

runAsUser.description: Run PB as the `pocketbase` user (uid 1000 in the image).

fsGroup.description: Group that owns the mounted volumes.

containerSecurityContext.description: Container-level securityContext. The root filesystem is read-only; /tmp is an emptyDir and /app/pb_data the PVC.

readOnlyRootFilesystem.description: Mount the container root filesystem read-only.

tag.description: Frontend image tag. Should match the RÝNI release.

pullPolicy.description: Image pull policy for the frontend. Empty falls back to `image.pullPolicy`.

type.description: Kubernetes service type for the frontend.

port.description: Port exposed by the frontend service. Default 8080 because the nginx-unprivileged image listens on 8080 (designed to run as non-root). Use 80 only if you switch to the standard nginx image and grant NET_BIND_SERVICE.

resources.description: Frontend container resources. nginx serving a static SPA needs little.

podSecurityContext.description: Pod-level securityContext for the frontend pod.

runAsUser.description: Run as the `nginx` user in nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged.

containerSecurityContext.description: Container-level securityContext. The root filesystem is read-only; nginx writes its pid/temp files to /tmp and /var/cache/nginx (both emptyDirs), and the runtime config (config.js) goes to /tmp/ryni written by the entrypoint at start.

readOnlyRootFilesystem.description: Mount the container root filesystem read-only.

rateLimit.description: nginx-level ingest rate limiting (defense-in-depth on top of PocketBase's built-in rate limiter, which is the authoritative one and is enabled by a migration). Auth brute-force is handled by PB. nginx sits behind the ingress, so to key on the real client IP it must trust the ingress as a proxy: set `realIpFrom` to the ingress controller's pod CIDR(s). Set `enabled` false to rely on PocketBase alone.

enabled.description: Enable the nginx ingest rate limit zone.

realIpFrom.description: Trusted proxy CIDRs for the nginx `real_ip` module (the ingress controller pods). Restrict to the cluster's pod CIDR for correctness.

realIpHeader.description: Header the ingress uses to carry the client IP.

ingestRate.description: Ingest rate per client IP, in nginx `limit_req_zone` notation (e.g. `240r/m`).

ingestBurst.description: Burst allowance for the ingest zone before requests are rejected.

networkPolicy.description: NetworkPolicies (require a CNI that enforces them, e.g. Calico, Cilium; without one they are inert). When enabled, PocketBase only accepts traffic on its HTTP port from the frontend pods (plus `pocketbase.extraFrom`); the frontend accepts traffic on its HTTP port from anywhere. Egress is not restricted (PB needs OIDC, SMTP if configured).

extraFrom.description: Additional `from` peers allowed to reach PocketBase (NetworkPolicy peer syntax), e.g. a monitoring namespace or a backup job. Each item is a free-form peer object.

ingress.description: Ingress configuration. Defaults to Traefik + cert-manager.

enabled.description: Whether to create an Ingress resource.

className.description: IngressClass name. `traefik` is the cluster's default.

annotations.description: Ingress annotations. The defaults issue a certificate via cert-manager and pin the Traefik websecure entrypoint.

hosts.description: Ingress hosts. Override the `host` field at install time.

paths.description: Paths routed to the frontend Service.

tls.description: TLS configuration. The cert-manager annotation above issues the cert.

secretName.description: Secret the issued certificate is stored in.
